source_refs.note: Topic 9.17 with Fig. 9.30 and the Point to ponder box (PDF 219-220, printed 216-217). The printed intermediate equations 9.48 to 9.50 are garbled, and the result is cited as Eq. 9.49; the lesson adds a potential-based explanation and records the finding.

blocks.text: The Wheatstone bridge (Fig. 9.30) is an electric circuit consisting of four resistances R1, R2, R3 and R4 connected so as to form a mesh ABCDA. A battery is connected between points A and C, and a sensitive galvanometer of resistance Rg is connected between points B and D. If the switch S is closed, a current will in general flow through the galvanometer. We have to determine the condition under which no current flows through the galvanometer even after the switch is closed.

blocks.alt: Four resistors R1, R2, R3 and R4 form a diamond ABCD. A galvanometer G joins B and D, and a cell joins A and C. A box says the bridge is balanced, with G reading zero, when R1 / R2 = R3 / R4.
blocks.caption: Wheatstone bridge circuit (original diagram after Figure 9.30).

blocks.text: Analysing the circuit with Kirchhoff's second rule, taking two loops ABDA and BCDB with anticlockwise loop currents I1 and I2: loop ABDA gives -I1 R1 - (I1 - I2) Rg - I1 R3 = 0 ... (9.46) and loop BCDB gives -I2 R2 - I2 R4 - (I2 - I1) Rg = 0 ... (9.47). The current through the galvanometer is zero if I1 - I2 = 0, that is I1 = I2, and the equations reduce to the balance condition R1/R2 = R3/R4 ... (9.51).

blocks.title: Balanced Wheatstone bridge
blocks.text: Whenever R1/R2 = R3/R4 ... (9.51) is satisfied, no current flows through the galvanometer and it shows no deflection; conversely, when the galvanometer shows no deflection, the condition is satisfied.

If three resistances R1, R2 and R3 of known, adjustable values and a fourth resistance R4 of unknown value are connected, and R1, R2 and R3 are adjusted until the galvanometer shows no deflection, the unknown resistance R4 can be determined from the known resistances by Eq. 9.51: R4 = R2 R3/R1.
